$comment: PLAN §13.5 load budgets, enforced in CI on the production build (gzip -9 sizes). vendor-three = three/webgpu (WebGPURenderer + WebGL2 backend + node/TSL system), measured 234 KB gz at three 0.186; 251.2 KB after the ≤150-programs work (ce218a1) pulled in more of the node/shadow system, so the cap is 256 KB. course-<id> = each course pack's data (one chunk per course) (docs/specs/COURSE-PACKS.md §2: its chapters, quests, labels, boards, market, models and lock), loaded with the voyage, never by the title (check-budgets fails if the entry imports it statically).

memory.$comment: tools/memorytest.mjs (npm run check:memory): GPU memory three tracks (renderer.info, made honest by engine/memory-ledger.ts) and the JS heap after GC, at each stop of two Anchorage → Meridian → Thousand-Bough → Anchorage round trips. Ceilings are the measured peaks plus ~15 %.

margin.$heapFloorMB: The heap may also grow this much (MB), whichever allows more: what a first voyage leaves behind for good doesn't scale with the heap. A heap-snapshot diff (first Anchorage vs a new voyage, High WebGPU) put ~7 MB of the ~10 MB in V8 compiled code for the island modules a voyage first loads (they never unload) and ~1 MB in kept CPU data (packs, caches); the same +10 MB at HEAD. A relative-only margin passed at 86 MB and failed once the grass freed its build data (69 MB).

leak.$trackedMB: Growth allowed from one round trip's Anchorage to the next (MB). It's only a leak signal if the reading doesn't depend on timing: three counted a texture once, at its size when first seen, so an image still decoding (5.3 MB per 1024² kit or terrain WebP) or TRAA's history target sized after its first use (11 MB at 1600 × 900) counted ~0 or in full by the luck of the frame, and the same stop read 453-484 MB on one tree (issue 261). The ledger now recounts a texture whose size changed (engine/memory-ledger.ts) and the test holds the render scale at the tier's (adaptive resolution would resize ~90 MB of screen targets on High). With issue 262 fixed (instanced meshes free the instance buffers three made for them), every round trip reads the same to 0.1 MB on High and Lite, WebGPU and WebGL2, and its resources match one for one; before it, High WebGPU grew 0.6 MB a round trip. 1 MB is ten times the jitter seen and still catches one leaked 512² texture with mips (1.3 MB) or ~8 instanced meshes' matrices a trip (128 KB each).

perf.$comment: tools/perftest.mjs (npm run check:perf), the local perf gate, per tier: main-thread ms per frame (Engine.cpuMs, median of a settled view's frames) with Chrome's CPU throttle at `throttle` (docs/specs/PHASE-0-spike.md §5: 3x on this M3 Max stands in for the UHD 620 floor), GPU ms per frame (WebGPU's pass-timestamp union, uncapped, at the tier's render scale and 1080p), and the Phase 0 flythrough's peak triangles in one frame. `target` is PLAN §12.1 / the spec's budget; `gate` is what the gate fails on: the target where it's met, else the worst reading measured on 2026-10-22 plus ~10 %, so nothing regresses while the target stands (Dan accepted these gaps on 2026-10-22, PLAN §12.1 and issues.md #29).

low.$gate: cpuMs: 7.0 ms worst (WebGL2, sailing; WebGPU 6.0 at the quay and sailing). gpuMs: 1.12 ms worst (Thousand-Bough's booths).

high.$gate: cpuMs: 4.7 ms worst (WebGPU, sailing). gpuMs: 4.15 ms worst (Thousand-Bough's booths).
